why: A world's surface is the top of a stack. Recipes are gated by axes and flags, not a name regex. Thicknesses are class numbers; ice-shell cells scale lid and ocean from the existing shell fields. Not a saved per-cell array and not deposition history.

layers.name: envelope
layers.why: Hydrogen–helium with no solid surface. Pressure is the vertical coordinate; this layer is the honest empty stack.

layers.name: organic sand
layers.why: Photochemical goo sitting on ice. Titan's dunes and Pluto's dark regions are this layer, metres thick, not bedrock.

layers.name: regolith
layers.why: Gardened dust on an airless world. Lunar mare regolith is a few metres; it mutes every crater rim.

layers.name: megaregolith
layers.why: Kilometres of impact-shattered crust. Porous, weak, and the reason lunar craters relax the way they do.

layers.name: ice lid
layers.why: Ice I shell. Europa 15–25 km; Enceladus thinner at the south pole. The lid is what a lander hits.

layers.name: subsurface ocean
layers.why: Liquid water under ice. Europa's ocean is ~100 km; it is the habitable layer and the thing plumes sample.

layers.name: ice VI
layers.why: High-pressure ice between a deep ocean and rock. Titan has it; Europa's smaller g keeps the ocean on rock.

layers.name: methane clathrate
layers.why: Cage ice holding methane. Titan's interior store; not a seafloor map. The tick still owns dissociation.

layers.name: lava crust
layers.why: A magma-ocean world has a thin chilled lid over melt, not a continent. Thickness is a sketch.

layers.name: rock
layers.why: Silicate basement. The ocean sits on it when g is too low for ice VI; the Moon's crust is ~40 km.

recipes.why: Giants and other envelopes have no heightfield to hang a column from. Pressure levels are the next pass.
A furnace world is a chilled lid over melt. Not Earth's crust, and not a stratigraphy.
Titan class: organic sand over ice I over an ammonia-rich ocean over ice VI over rock. Gates are CH4 plus an atmosphere, not /titan/.
Europa class: ice over ocean over rock. Ice VI only when seafloor pressure demands it. Lid and ocean thicknesses follow the shell fields.
Io's lithosphere is a thin silicate lid continually buried by lava. Sulfur is cover, not a column layer.
Moon class: metres of gardened dust over kilometres of shattered crust over ~40 km of basement. Mercury and the other airless rocks share it.
A generic solid world has crust. Cover and landforms sit on top; deposition history is not this cut.
